correctness.rationale: Exact algebra in basis (p_i,e_i) gives \(V_i=\Delta_i(r-1)\), \(\dot r=-a(r-1)\) and \(\dot u=[\omega_i+a(u-1/2)(r-1)]/r\). The universal strict positivity bound for \(0<r<1+2\min_i\omega_i/a\) gives unique non-Zeno crossings and forward invariance. The event equation has a strictly increasing left-minus-right side and a unique positive root. The radial law proves all-interior and collar attraction, restricts every periodic orbit to \(r=1\), and gives the Poincare transverse multiplier \(e^{-aT}\). Identical coordinate equations and boundary gluing prove time-preserving conjugacy between any two shapes. Independent symbolic identities and direct physical 2D affine integrations corroborate the calculation in the embedded verify.py. Limits at the origin, outside the radial domain, and in other parameter families are explicitly excluded.

value.rationale: The problem of preserving temporal response when changing polygonal oscillator geometry is natural in trajectory synthesis and switched systems. The simultaneous tuning is nontrivial for arbitrary star-shaped polygon vertex data and produces an exact shape-independent finite-time hybrid flow, not just the familiar invariant polygon or per-sector contraction. It proves a large punctured-interior basin and a quantified exterior crossing bound, and supplies an exact event-time return law useful for testing numerical hybrid oscillators. The chosen parameters are geometrically motivated by cancelling polygon terms, not an arbitrary slice or a routine replacement of a symbol.
